audit.whatIsWrong: diff says HARD but tone is the favourable green, diffRating is 4/10 and both difficulty lines read 'Favoured matchup' — at a 33.33% win rate. Two chart rows also disagree with the packet and with their own whys: Level 6 renders Neeko while whys[4] calls it 'a genuine coinflip window', and 2+ items renders Dr. Mundo while whys[6] says 'it evens out off the 1v1'.
audit.why: A 33% matchup was being presented to the player as favoured, in green, at 4/10.
audit.corrected: diffRating 7/10, carryRating 7/10, tone to the hard colour, both difficulty lines to 'Hard matchup'; Level 6 and 2+ items set to Skill as matched full/content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0] through phases[6] carried boilerplate naming no Dr. Mundo ability, and phases[5] referenced a Stormsurge spike the content layer does not build.
audit.why: The spike timeline is his: Infected Bonesaw on a 4s cooldown from level 2, Heart Zapper's stored-damage heal, and Maximum Dosage's flat 120s heal at 6.
audit.corrected: All seven rewritten on those cooldowns and on the passive.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup is absent from every field: Goes Where He Pleases resists the FIRST immobilizing effect that hits him, converting it into a health cost and a cannister. Neeko's entire pattern is Tangle-Barbs root into Pop Blossom stun — both are immobilizing, and the page tells the player to build the all-in around a root that will simply be eaten. Separately, mid tells you to use 'disguise/clone and invisibility', which Neeko does not have.
audit.why: Every all-in the page recommends assumes the root lands. Against this passive the correct play is to spend E early specifically to strip it, then commit with the second piece of CC.
audit.corrected: report[5].t, dosFull[2] and phases[2].why rebuilt on the passive; the invisibility claim removed from mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d offered a 'fifteen-second invitation' after Heart Zapper and dosFull[2].t said to save E to interrupt it.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s and nothing in its description makes it interruptible; Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s at every rank, which is the number the level-6 all-in actually hangs on.
audit.corrected: 17s written into dosFull[2].d, the flat 120s into phases[4].why and mid, and dosFull[2] retitled to spending E on the passive.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1], early and wants.foe[0] all call his Q 'Infected Cleaver'.

edits.before: Level 1 is your only clean poke window — your single-target Q (Blooming Burst) chunks him before his passive starts healing off minion kills, so land it and back off. The moment he gets a couple of points in his cleaver, his Q (Infected Cleaver) percent-HP pokes you for more than you return and self-heals, and he has the HP pool to ignore your seed. Do not throw E (Tangle-Barbs) as a poke here — whiff it and you're naked in cleaver range with no escape. Last-hit at max Q range and respect that he wants this lane to go long.
edits.after: Level 1 is your only clean poke window — your single-target Q (Blooming Burst) chunks him before his passive regen and cannisters start carrying him, so land it and back off. The moment he gets a couple of points in it, his Q (Infected Bonesaw) percent-health pokes you every 4 seconds for more than you return, and he has the HP pool to ignore your seed. Do not throw E (Tangle-Barbs) as a poke — his passive eats the first immobilizing effect anyway, and a whiff leaves you naked in bonesaw range. Last-hit at max Q range; he wants this lane long.

edits.before: Through Levels 4-5 you're just farming with Q re-blooms while he stacks cleaver heals and outpaces your poke — this is his lane to grind. Level 6 hands you your one real threat: a landed E into Q and Pop Blossom can delete him IF his R (Maximum Dosage) is down, so track his ult and only commit on its cooldown. If you slam Pop Blossom into a full-HP Mundo with R available, he heals straight through it and walks you down. Honestly your best mid-game is using disguise/clone and invisibility to leave this lane and gank — you make plays elsewhere, not here.
edits.after: Through Levels 4-5 you're just farming with Q re-blooms while Heart Zapper heals back what you chip — this is his lane to grind. Level 6 hands you your one real threat: a landed E into Q and Pop Blossom can delete him IF his R (Maximum Dosage) is down, so track its flat 120 seconds and only commit on that. If you slam Pop Blossom into a full-HP Mundo with R available, he heals straight through it and walks you down. Honestly your best mid-game is disguising as an ally and leaving this lane to gank — you make plays elsewhere, not here.

notes: The biggest omission in my slice is here: Goes Where He Pleases resists the FIRST immobilizing effect that hits Dr. Mundo. Neeko's whole pattern is root into stun, and nothing on the page said her opener gets eaten. The correct sequencing — spend Tangle-Barbs early purely to strip the passive, then commit Pop Blossom — is now in report[5].t, dosFull[2] and phases[2].why. The page was also presenting a 33.33% matchup as 'Favoured, 4/10' in green while its own diff field said HARD. 'Infected Cleaver' was the wrong Q name in three fields.
